chunks: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam al-Kulayni and 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated from 'Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), 'What is the meaning of the One?'
He answered, 'He is the One upon whom all tongues agree in affirming Divine Unity,'
as Allah, the Mighty and High, says: 'And if you ask them, Who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the theological definition of 'The One' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this definition to highlight that Divine Unity is not merely an intellectual abstraction but a universally recognized reality, even among polytheists when pressed for the ultimate source of creation. By citing Surah Luqman, the text underscores the consensus of the human soul (Fitrah) in acknowledging Allah as the sole Creator, distinguishing this primary Tawhid from the more complex theological attributes of God.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 2. Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isam al-Kulayni; and `Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Imran al-Daqqaq (RA) both said: Muhammad ibn Ya`qub al-Kulayni, on the authority of `Ali ibn Muhammad said; and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan all of whom on the authority of Sahl ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Hashim al-Ja`fari that I asked Abu `Jafar the Second (AS), “What is the meaning of the One?”
He answered, “He is the One whose Divine Unity [al-Tawhid] is profess by all.
As Allah, the Mighty and High, says: And if you as them, Who created the Heavens and the Earth, they will certainly say, Allah.1
